symbols.name: I
symbols.def: \(I_T\) is the nonstochastic regime indicator for intervention on \(T\).

symbols.name: COPAG0
symbols.def: The input-free COPAG class of Chen--Mooij.

symbols.name: PAG
symbols.def: \(\mathcal P=(\varnothing,V,E)\).

symbols.name: mBuckets
symbols.def: \(m_{\mathfrak B}\) is the number of buckets of \(\mathcal P\).

symbols.name: Buckets
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak B(\mathcal P)=(B_1,\ldots,B_{m_{\mathfrak B}})\) is a fixed deterministic ordering of the buckets of \(\mathcal P\).
symbols.role: Defines the role intersections considered by the branch search.

symbols.name: W
symbols.def: \(W=X\cup C\).
symbols.role: Coordinates that may exchange treatment and conditioning roles.

symbols.name: S
symbols.def: The selected cohort is the event \(S=\mathbf 1\).

symbols.name: Mdplus
symbols.def: The positive discrete selected-SCM class represented by \(\mathcal P\) in Chen--Mooij.

symbols.name: M
symbols.role: Generic model in the published identification domain.

symbols.name: Ma
symbols.role: First generic model in the definition of identification.

symbols.name: Mb
symbols.role: Second generic model in the definition of identification.

symbols.name: Pobs
symbols.def: \(P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M}=P_{\mathbf M}(V\mid S=\mathbf 1)\).

symbols.name: psi
symbols.def: \(\psi_{\mathbf M}(y;x,c)=P_{\mathbf M}(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x),C=c,S=\mathbf 1)\).

symbols.name: rho
symbols.def: \(\rho=(\bar X,\bar C)\) with \(\bar X\mathbin{\dot\cup}\bar C=W\).

symbols.name: Omega
symbols.def: \(\Omega(\mathcal P;Y,X,C)\) is rooted at \((X,C)\) and contains exactly states reachable through legal bucket-intersection Rule-2 exchanges.

symbols.name: sIDP
symbols.def: Chen--Mooij's sound and complete unconditional selected-kernel algorithm for input-free COPAGs.

symbols.name: CIDP
symbols.def: The complete no-selection conditional-PAG algorithm of Jaber--Ribeiro--Zhang--Bareinboim.

symbols.name: J
symbols.def: \(J_{\rho,\mathbf M}(y,\bar c;\bar x)=P_{\mathbf M}(Y=y,\bar C=\bar c\mid\operatorname{do}(\bar X=\bar x),S=\mathbf 1)\).

symbols.name: D
symbols.def: \(D_{\rho,\mathbf M}(\bar c;\bar x)=\sum_{y'\in\{0,1\}^Y}J_{\rho,\mathbf M}(y',\bar c;\bar x)\).
symbols.role: Quantity held fixed by a locked certificate.

symbols.name: N
symbols.def: \(N_{\rho,\mathbf M}(y,\bar c;\bar x)=J_{\rho,\mathbf M}(y,\bar c;\bar x)\).
symbols.role: Quantity separated by a locked certificate.

symbols.name: Frho
symbols.def: \(F_{\rho}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) is the formula returned by sIDP for \(J_{\rho}\), when that call succeeds.
symbols.role: Numerator functional on a successful branch.

symbols.name: Branch
symbols.role: Returns a normalized symbolic formula or \(\operatorname{AllFail}\).

symbols.name: Mrep
symbols.role: MAG component of a graphical certificate.

symbols.name: Grep
symbols.type: represented selected acyclic directed mixed graph
symbols.role: Selected graphical realization of a certificate.

symbols.name: F
symbols.role: Larger forest in a terminal selected hedge.

symbols.name: Fprime
symbols.def: \(F'\subsetneq F\).
symbols.role: Smaller forest in a terminal selected hedge.

symbols.name: Rroot
symbols.def: \(R_F\) is the common root set of \(F\) and \(F'\).
symbols.role: Root coordinate of a selected hedge.

symbols.name: Gamma
symbols.def: \(\Gamma=(\rho,\mathcal M,\mathcal G,F,F',R_F,\mathbf M_0,\mathbf M_1)\) together with a legal role trace and expanded rational evaluation tables.

symbols.name: Mbase
symbols.role: Base point of an affine mechanism family.

symbols.name: dtheta
symbols.def: \(d_{\theta}\) is the number of entries in the varied local conditional-probability table.

symbols.name: Simplex
symbols.def: \(\Delta_{\theta}\) is the product of simplices determined by the conditioning blocks of the varied local table.
symbols.role: Normalization domain for the varied mechanism.

symbols.name: theta
symbols.def: \(\theta\) is one normalized local conditional-probability table of \(\mathbf M_{\mathrm{base}}\).
symbols.role: Mechanism varied by the affine template.

symbols.name: T
symbols.def: \(T=\{w\in\mathbb Q^{d_{\theta}}:\sum_{j\text{ in each probability block}}w_j=0\}\).

symbols.name: Rmat
symbols.def: The columns of \(R_T\) form a rational basis of \(T\).

symbols.name: Mfamily
symbols.def: \(\mathbf M(t)\) replaces the local table \(\theta\) of \(\mathbf M_{\mathrm{base}}\) by \(\theta+t v\) and leaves every other mechanism unchanged.

symbols.name: oz
symbols.def: \(o_z(t)=P_{\mathbf M(t)}(V=z,S=\mathbf 1)\).

symbols.name: Zo
symbols.def: \(Z_o(t)=\sum_z o_z(t)\).

symbols.name: h
symbols.def: \(h(t)=P_{\mathbf M(t)}(\bar C=\bar c,S=\mathbf 1\mid\operatorname{do}(\bar X=\bar x))\).

symbols.name: k
symbols.def: \(k(t)=P_{\mathbf M(t)}(Y=y,\bar C=\bar c,S=\mathbf 1\mid\operatorname{do}(\bar X=\bar x))\).

symbols.name: Zx
symbols.def: \(Z_x(t)=P_{\mathbf M(t)}(S=\mathbf 1\mid\operatorname{do}(\bar X=\bar x))\).

symbols.name: Aobs
symbols.def: Its row for cell \(z\) is the coefficient map \(w\mapsto Z_o(0)\,\delta_w o_z-o_z(0)\,\delta_w Z_o\).
symbols.role: Locks the complete normalized selected observational law.

symbols.name: drow
symbols.def: \(d:w\mapsto Z_x(0)\,\delta_w h-h(0)\,\delta_w Z_x\).

symbols.name: brow
symbols.def: \(b:w\mapsto Z_x(0)\,\delta_w k-k(0)\,\delta_w Z_x\).
symbols.role: Detects change in the terminal selected numerator.

symbols.name: E
symbols.def: \(E=\begin{bmatrix}A_{\mathrm{obs}}\\ d\end{bmatrix}\).

symbols.name: LockCompile
symbols.role: Turns a passing affine template into an explicit model pair.

symbols.name: Ltemp
symbols.def: \(L_{\mathrm{temp}}\) is the binary bit length of the rational base mechanisms, represented graph and forest data, query, and matrices \(E_T,b_T\).

symbols.name: Lcert
symbols.def: \(L_{\Gamma}\) is the bit length of the graph objects, rational mechanisms, dense full-assignment tables, and arithmetic trace in \(\Gamma\).

symbols.name: Verify
symbols.role: Checks representation, forest predicates, factorization, and exact probability equalities.

symbols.name: Ui
symbols.def: \(U_i\) is the common cause in the informative-lock construction.

symbols.name: Dinf
symbols.def: \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{inf}}\) has edges \(U_i\to X_i,U_i\to Y_i,X_i\to Y_i,Y_i\to C_i,Y_i\to S_i,C_i\to S_i\).
symbols.role: Underlying graph of the informative exact witness.

symbols.name: Ginf
symbols.def: \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{inf}}\) has \(X_i\to Y_i,X_i\leftrightarrow Y_i,Y_i\to C_i,Y_i\to S_i,C_i\to S_i\).

symbols.name: MinfMAG
symbols.def: \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{inf}}\) is the observed MAG \(X_i-Y_i-C_i\) with both edges undirected and no \(X_i-C_i\) edge.
symbols.role: Selected latent projection on the observed vertices.

symbols.name: Pinf
symbols.def: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{inf}}\) is the chain \(X_i\mathbin{\circ\!-\!\circ}Y_i\mathbin{\circ\!-\!\circ}C_i\).
symbols.role: COPAG represented by the informative MAG.

symbols.name: Finf
symbols.def: \(F_{\mathrm{inf}}=(\{X_i,Y_i\},\{X_i\to Y_i,X_i\leftrightarrow Y_i\})\).
symbols.role: Larger forest for the terminal joint target.

symbols.name: Finfprime
symbols.def: \(F'_{\mathrm{inf}}=(\{Y_i\},\varnothing)\).

symbols.name: Rinf
symbols.def: \(R_{\mathrm{inf}}=\{Y_i\}\).

symbols.name: DmaxInf
symbols.def: \(D_{\max,\mathrm{inf}}=\varnothing\) for the informative terminal query.
symbols.role: Selection-exchange coordinate in the explicit hedge check.

symbols.name: Alt
symbols.def: \(\widetilde P(S_i=1\mid Y_i=1,C_i=1)=1/2\), with the other informative-witness mechanisms unchanged.
symbols.role: Shows that denominator equality is not imposed by the graph.

symbols.name: Ub
symbols.def: \(U_b\) is the common cause in the isolated-bow baseline.

symbols.name: Diso
symbols.def: \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{iso}}\) has edges \(U_b\to X_b,U_b\to Y_b,X_b\to Y_b,Y_b\to S_b\), with \(C_b\) isolated.
symbols.role: Graph of the vacuous-denominator regression baseline.

symbols.name: Hlock
symbols.role: Concrete starting move for the open graph-to-rank construction.

symbols.name: formulaDAG
symbols.role: Cache of region decompositions, fixing attempts, and repeated subexpressions.

symbols.name: Lformula
symbols.def: \(L_{\mathrm{form}}\) is the bit length of the shared formula DAG returned by Branch-sCIDP.

symbols.name: PAGId
symbols.def: The public implementation of no-selection IDP and CIDP.

standard.name: Disjoint treatment, outcome, and conditioning sets
Positive discrete selected SCM represented by a COPAG

assumptions.condition: Every endogenous and latent variable of \(\mathbf M\) is binary.

novel.justification: Binary treatments, outcomes, eligibility variables, and latent response types are standard finite approximations in selected-cohort analyses and form the first nontrivial exact certificate class.

assumptions.condition: Every local stochastic-mechanism entry of \(\mathbf M\) is rational and strictly between zero and one.

novel.justification: Finite rational probability tables cover recorded designs and discretized scientific mechanisms, are dense in the positive table simplex, and allow a countermodel certificate to be reproduced with exact arithmetic.

definitions.name: Positive rational binary certificate class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{rat,bin}}^+(\mathcal P)=\{\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M_d^+(\mathcal P):\text{ every endogenous and latent variable is binary and every local mechanism entry is rational and lies in }(0,1)\}\).

definitions.name: Identification over the published selected model class
definitions.construction: \(\psi\) is identified if \(P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M_a}=P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M_b}\) implies \(\psi_{\mathbf M_a}=\psi_{\mathbf M_b}\) for every \(\mathbf M_a,\mathbf M_b\in\mathfrak M_d^+(\mathcal P)\).

definitions.name: Reachable role-state graph
definitions.construction: Start at \(\rho_0=(X,C)\). For every bucket \(B_j\), move the nonempty current role intersection \(B_j\cap\bar X\) from \(\bar X\) to \(\bar C\), or move \(B_j\cap\bar C\) in the reverse direction, exactly when the corresponding Chen--Mooij Rule-2 separation with regime indicator \(I_T\) holds; retain every reachable state and edge.

definitions.name: Branch-sCIDP
definitions.construction: Enumerate \(\Omega(\mathcal P;Y,X,C)\). At each \(\rho=(\bar X,\bar C)\), run sIDP on \(J_{\rho}=P(Y,\bar C\mid\operatorname{do}(\bar X),S=\mathbf 1)\). On the first successful deterministic state, return \(F_{\rho}(y,\bar c;\bar x;P_{\mathrm{obs}})/\sum_{y'}F_{\rho}(y',\bar c;\bar x;P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), restoring the original assignments along the trace; otherwise return \(\operatorname{AllFail}\).

definitions.name: Denominator-locked selected conditional certificate
definitions.construction: \(\Gamma\) contains a reachable terminal state \(\rho\), a represented \(\mathcal M\in[\mathcal P]_{\mathsf M}\), a represented \(\mathcal G\in[\mathcal M]_{\mathsf G}\), nested \(R_F\)-rooted C-forests \(F'\subsetneq F\) satisfying the terminal selected-hedge predicates for the entire terminal intervention, and \(\mathbf M_0,\mathbf M_1\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{rat,bin}}^+(\mathcal P)\) with equal full selected observational laws, \(D_{\rho,\mathbf M_0}=D_{\rho,\mathbf M_1}>0\), and \(N_{\rho,\mathbf M_0}\neq N_{\rho,\mathbf M_1}\), together with dense exact rational tables.

definitions.name: One-mechanism affine rational family
definitions.construction: Fix represented coordinates \(\mathcal M\in[\mathcal P]_{\mathsf M}\), \(\mathcal G\in[\mathcal M]_{\mathsf G}\), and nested \(R_F\)-rooted forests \(F'\subsetneq F\) satisfying the terminal selected-hedge predicates. Choose one local table \(\theta\) of \(\mathbf M_{\mathrm{base}}\), a rational simplex-tangent direction \(v=R_Tq\), and define \(\mathbf M(t)\) by replacing \(\theta\) with \(\theta+t v\) while holding every other local mechanism fixed.

definitions.name: Observational-and-denominator lock system
definitions.construction: For the affine family, form the observational rows \(A_{\mathrm{obs},z}:w\mapsto Z_o(0)\delta_w o_z-o_z(0)\delta_w Z_o\), the denominator row \(d:w\mapsto Z_x(0)\delta_w h-h(0)\delta_w Z_x\), and the numerator row \(b:w\mapsto Z_x(0)\delta_w k-k(0)\delta_w Z_x\). Set \(E=[A_{\mathrm{obs}};d]\), \(E_T=ER_T\), and \(b_T=bR_T\).

definitions.name: Exact lock compiler
definitions.construction: Apply rational row reduction to \(E_T\) and \(b_T\); when the augmented-rank test passes, select a rational \(q\in\ker(E_T)\) with \(b_Tq\neq0\), set \(v=R_Tq\), choose a nonzero rational \(t\) inside the exact positivity radius, and expand the supplied represented graph and forest data together with \(\mathbf M(0),\mathbf M(t)\) into \(\Gamma\).

definitions.name: Informative denominator-lock mechanisms
definitions.construction: On \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{inf}}\), set \(P(U_i=1)=1/2\), \(P(X_i=1\mid U_i=0)=1/4\), \(P(X_i=1\mid U_i=1)=3/4\), and \(P_{\sigma}(Y_i=1\mid X_i=a,U_i=u)=1/2+\sigma(u-r_a)/4\). Set \(P(C_i=1\mid Y_i=0)=1/4\), \(P(C_i=1\mid Y_i=1)=3/4\), and \(P(S_i=1\mid Y_i=b,C_i=d)=1/4\) when \(b=d\) and \(3/4\) otherwise. All Bernoulli complements use one minus the displayed entry; \(\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},+}\) and \(\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},-}\) use \(\sigma=+1\) and \(\sigma=-1\).

definitions.name: Informative graph and forest coordinates
definitions.construction: Use \(V=\{X_i,Y_i,C_i\}\), \(S=\{S_i\}\), \(X=\{X_i\}\), \(Y=\{Y_i\}\), \(C=\{C_i\}\), \(x(X_i)=0\), \(y(Y_i)=1\), \(c(C_i)=1\), the root state \(\rho=(\{X_i\},\{C_i\})\), \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{inf}}\), \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{inf}}\), \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{inf}}\), \(F_{\mathrm{inf}}\), \(F'_{\mathrm{inf}}\), \(R_{\mathrm{inf}}\), and \(D_{\max,\mathrm{inf}}=\varnothing\).

definitions.name: Vacuous-denominator bow baseline
definitions.construction: On \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{iso}}\), set \(P(U_b=1)=P(C_b=1)=1/2\), \(P(X_b=1\mid U_b=0)=1/4\), \(P(X_b=1\mid U_b=1)=3/4\), \(P_{\sigma}(Y_b=1\mid X_b=a,U_b=u)=1/2+\sigma(u-r^b_a)/4\), \(P(S_b=1\mid Y_b=0)=1/3\), and \(P(S_b=1\mid Y_b=1)=2/3\). The models \(\mathbf M_{\mathrm{iso},+}\) and \(\mathbf M_{\mathrm{iso},-}\) use the two signs.

definitions.name: Residual-forest-to-lock handle
definitions.construction: From the shared role graph, choose a deterministic maximal-intervention all-fail terminal state, extract Chen--Mooij's residual region and represented selected forest for that complete terminal intervention, parameterize a rational interior one-forest mechanism table, compute \(E_T\) and \(b_T\), and, only if the rank test fails, enlarge to a two-mechanism rational tangent space before testing again.

definitions.name: Shared Branch-sCIDP formula cache
definitions.construction: For each observed subset, cache its deterministic selected-region decomposition, fixing attempt, identified kernel, and assembly node once; every terminal state requests its anterior region and final marginalization from this shared formula DAG.

statements.statement: Every symbolic formula returned by \(\operatorname{Branch\text{-}sCIDP}(\mathcal P;Y,X,C)\) equals \(\psi_{\mathbf M}(y;x,c)\) for every \(\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M_d^+(\mathcal P)\). The role graph has at most \(2^{|X\cup C|}\) states, every nonrepeating trace has length at most \(2^{|X\cup C|}-1\), and the shared formula DAG can be constructed in \(O(3^n\operatorname{poly}(n)+L_{\mathrm{form}})\) symbolic operations. No implication from \(\operatorname{AllFail}\) to nonidentification is asserted here.
statements.justification: Exhaustive legal exchanges preserve the target and isolate the converse difficulty without sacrificing a usable positive identification procedure.
statements.gap: Chen--Mooij prove soundness for their conditional procedure; the branch closure and shared-cache accounting are not stated as this explicit formula-search theorem.
statements.consumer: PAGId can return selected-cohort formulas with a finite auditable role trace even before a complete failure theorem is available.

statements.statement: For every rational interior one-mechanism affine family, the following are equivalent: \(\exists q\in\mathbb Q^{\dim(T)}\) with \(E_Tq=0\) and \(b_Tq\neq0\); and \(\operatorname{rank}([E_T;b_T])>\operatorname{rank}(E_T)\). The condition is independent of the rational basis \(R_T\). Whenever it holds, rational row reduction yields \(v=R_Tq\), and there is a computable \(\delta\in\mathbb Q_{>0}\) such that every \(t\in\mathbb Q\) with \(0<|t|<\delta\) keeps \(\theta+t v\) normalized and strictly positive, preserves the entire normalized selected observational law and \(D_{\rho}\) exactly, and changes \(N_{\rho}\). Thus \(\operatorname{LockCompile}\) returns a positive rational pair certifying nonidentification of \(\psi\) in \(\operatorname{poly}(L_{\mathrm{temp}}+L_{\Gamma})\) bit operations, and \(\operatorname{Verify}\) checks the expanded certificate in \(\operatorname{poly}(|\mathcal P|+L_{\Gamma})\) bit operations.
statements.justification: The theorem turns a numerical or symbolic fiber direction into an exact, portable, positive rational causal nonidentification certificate.
statements.gap: Discrete polynomial programs describe observational fibers, but the checked literature does not isolate an exact simplex-tangent criterion that simultaneously locks a selected conditional denominator and separates its numerator.
statements.consumer: A graph search or algebraic solver can hand one passing template to the compiler and obtain a certificate that a third party verifies without trusting the search.

statements.statement: The mechanisms in \(\text{def:informative-lock-template}\) are strictly positive and rational and induce \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{inf}}\), whose latent projections are \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{inf}}\) and \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{inf}}=X_i-Y_i-C_i\), with \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{inf}}\in\operatorname{COPAG}_0(\{X_i,Y_i,C_i\})\), \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{inf}}\in[\mathcal P_{\mathrm{inf}}]_{\mathsf M}\), and \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{inf}}\in[\mathcal M_{\mathrm{inf}}]_{\mathsf G}\). Both models therefore belong to \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{rat,bin}}^+(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{inf}})\). Moreover \(P_{\sigma}(U_i=1\mid X_i=a)=r_a\) and \(P_{\sigma}(Y_i=1\mid X_i=a)=1/2\), while \(P(C_i=d,S_i=1\mid Y_i=b)=3/16\) for every \(b,d\in\{0,1\}\). Hence \(P_{\sigma}(X_i=a,Y_i=b,C_i=d,S_i=1)=3/64\), \(P_{\sigma}(S_i=1)=3/8\), and the two full selected observational laws assign probability \(1/8\) to every observed cell. Under \(\operatorname{do}(X_i=0)\), \(P_+(Y_i=1)=9/16\), \(P_-(Y_i=1)=7/16\), and both selection normalizers equal \(3/8\). At the root role state, \(D_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},+}}(1;0)=D_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},-}}(1;0)=1/2\), whereas \(N_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},+}}(1,1;0)=9/32\) and \(N_{\rho,\mathbf M_{\mathrm{inf},-}}(1,1;0)=7/32\), so the conditional effects are \(9/16\) and \(7/16\). The connected \(C_i\) is informative before selection because \(P(C_i=1\mid Y_i=1)=3/4\neq1/4=P(C_i=1\mid Y_i=0)\). The pair \((F_{\mathrm{inf}},F'_{\mathrm{inf}})\) consists of nested \(R_{\mathrm{inf}}\)-rooted C-forests, with \(V(F_{\mathrm{inf}})\cap\{X_i\}=\{X_i\}\), \(V(F'_{\mathrm{inf}})\cap\{X_i\}=\varnothing\), and \(R_{\mathrm{inf}}\subseteq\operatorname{An}_{\mathcal G_{\mathrm{inf}},\operatorname{do}(X_i)}(\{Y_i,C_i,S_i\})\); \(D_{\max,\mathrm{inf}}=\varnothing\), so they form the terminal selected hedge for \((\{Y_i,C_i,S_i\},\{X_i\})\). Finally, replacing only \(P(S_i=1\mid Y_i=1,C_i=1)\) by \(1/2\) preserves the graph and equality of the two selected observational laws but yields denominators \(25/41\) and \(23/39\); therefore the displayed denominator equality is a tuned informative cancellation, not a structural consequence of the graph.
statements.justification: The explicit table proves that denominator locking can survive genuinely informative conditioning and selection without being imposed by graph separation or isolation.
statements.gap: Existing selected hedges separate interventional kernels but do not exhibit a connected conditioning coordinate with exact full-law equality, a positive equal denominator, an unequal numerator, and a same-graph nonlocking perturbation.
statements.consumer: The example is a mandatory positive-control certificate for implementations of rational selected-hedge synthesis and verification.

statements.statement: For the isolated-bow baseline, \(P_{\sigma}(X_b=a,C_b=d,Y_b=1,S_b=1)=1/12\), \(P_{\sigma}(X_b=a,C_b=d,Y_b=0,S_b=1)=1/24\), and \(P_{\sigma}(S_b=1)=1/2\), so the two full selected observational laws agree. Under \(\operatorname{do}(X_b=0)\), the unselected outcome probabilities are \(9/16\) and \(7/16\), the selection normalizers are \(25/48\) and \(23/48\), the joint numerators at \(Y_b=C_b=1\) are \(9/25\) and \(7/23\), and the conditional effects are \(18/25\) and \(14/23\). However \(D_{\rho}=1/2\) in both models solely because \(C_b\) is an isolated fair root. This proposition is a vacuous-denominator regression baseline and supplies no evidence for generic denominator locking.
statements.justification: Keeping the exact calculation visible prevents a structurally automatic denominator from being mistaken for evidence about informative conditioning.
statements.gap: The baseline was previously used as support for denominator locking even though isolation makes the denominator equality automatic.
statements.consumer: Certificate tests must classify this example as numerically valid but noninformative about the open graph-to-lock step.

statements.statement: Whenever every \(\rho\in\Omega(\mathcal P;Y,X,C)\) fails its terminal sIDP call, does the handle \(H_{\mathrm{lock}}(\mathcal P;Y,X,C,\Omega)\) produce a represented residual forest and a rational interior one- or two-mechanism observational-fiber tangent satisfying \(E_Tq=0\) and \(b_Tq\neq0\), or another explicit positive rational construction with the same full selected observational law and the same positive terminal denominator but a different terminal numerator? Can such an object be streamed in \(O(3^n\operatorname{poly}(n)+L_{\Gamma})\) bit operations?
statements.justification: This is the exact missing bridge from graphical failure to a reusable nonidentification certificate; neither ordinary hedge disagreement nor semantic nonidentifiability supplies the denominator lock automatically.
statements.gap: Chen--Mooij's residual-forest converse is unconditional, while no checked conditional-PAG or selected-hedge result coordinates all reachable role states and an informative selected denominator.
statements.consumer: A positive answer upgrades Branch-sCIDP from a sound formula search to a formula-or-checkable-failure decision procedure for selected-cohort PAG analysis.

statements.statement: When \(S=\varnothing\), Branch-sCIDP and CIDP agree on the identification decision for \(P_{\mathbf M}(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x),C=c)\), and every successful Branch-sCIDP formula is algebraically equivalent to a CIDP identifying functional.
statements.justification: The no-selection special case is the required regression against the settled conditional-PAG boundary.
statements.gap: This is a sanity reduction rather than a novelty claim; it rules out a selected extension that changes the established no-selection answer.
statements.consumer: PAGId retains its current CIDP behavior whenever no selection node is present.

sampling_model.design: One selected observational law \(P(V\mid S=\mathbf 1)\) generated by a positive discrete SCM represented by an input-free COPAG.
sampling_model.units: Identification compares structural models that induce the same complete selected observational distribution.
sampling_model.treatment: The intervention fixes \(X=x\); legal Rule-2 exchanges may reallocate coordinates between \(X\) and \(C\).
sampling_model.overlap: The published positive discrete model class makes every displayed selected conditioning stratum well defined.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None; the contribution is graphical identification and exact rational certificate synthesis rather than sampling inference.

estimand_functional: \(\psi(y;x,c)=F_{\rho}(y,\bar c;\bar x;P_{\mathrm{obs}})\big/\sum_{y'}F_{\rho}(y',\bar c;\bar x;P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) on a successful branch; on a passing affine failure template, \(E_Tq=0\) and \(b_Tq\neq0\) certify nonidentification.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The selected conditional procedure is sound, while conditional completeness is left to future work.
A sufficient graphical condition and a sound algorithm address \(P_X(Y\mid S=1)\) in one known augmented ADMG with latent variables.
Discrete causal questions reduce to polynomial programs that yield sharp or epsilon-sharp bounds.
Conditional interventional distributions have a necessary-and-sufficient identification criterion for a specified semi-Markovian graph.
CIDP is sound and complete for conditional causal-effect identification from PAGs without selection.
Graphical and formula-specific positivity conditions can license identifying formulas without global strict positivity.

tldr: The proposal replaces an overinterpreted isolated-conditioning bow with a reusable exact denominator-lock framework. Branch-sCIDP remains a sound finite formula search. Given a rational interior affine SCM template, a simplex-tangent rank inequality is necessary and sufficient for an exact positive rational pair with the same full selected observational law and selected conditioning denominator but different joint numerators, and the pair is compilable and checkable in polynomial time relative to its explicit encoding. A connected binary construction with \(Y_i\to C_i\) and \(C_i\to S_i\) realizes the lock by tuned informative selection cancellation, yields conditional effects \(9/16\) and \(7/16\), and admits a same-graph perturbation with unequal denominators. Whether every all-branches failure supplies such a forest tangent remains the explicit open question.

project_justification.gap: Selected conditional identification can fail at every joint-identification branch, yet ordinary selected hedges need not preserve the conditioning denominator and an isolated conditioning root makes preservation vacuous.
project_justification.niche: An exact algebraic certificate layer can be useful before full graphical completeness: it must distinguish graph representation, observational-fiber equality, denominator locking, and numerator separation, and it must demonstrate the lock with an informative conditioning variable.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies an if-and-only-if tangent-rank compiler, a complete connected rational witness with a same-graph nonlocking perturbation, and a sharply delimited residual-forest-to-rank question whose resolution would finish formula-or-certificate completeness.

related_work: Chen and Mooij provide the selected-COPAG model, complete unconditional sIDP, and sound conditional sCIDP; their work informs the role search and residual-forest handle, but no strict theorem comparison is claimed until the open graph-to-lock step is solved. Abouei and coauthors formulate selected hedges for one known augmented ADMG and an unconditional selected intervention target; their construction informs the forest coordinate but does not address postintervention conditioning or COPAG uncertainty. Duarte and coauthors show that finite discrete causal fibers are polynomially representable and computationally searchable; the present rank system focuses on exact local rational compilation rather than sharp-bound optimization. Shpitser and Pearl give the complete fixed-graph conditional benchmark, and Jaber and coauthors give its no-selection PAG counterpart; both motivate exhaustive exchange before joint identification. Hwang and coauthors motivate formula-specific treatment of positivity and cancellation. Chen, Zoeter, and Mooij provide the selected-SCM semantics used by both members of every certificate.
honest_scope: The proposal makes no claim that \(\operatorname{AllFail}\) implies a passing tangent. The exact rank equivalence is conditional on a specified rational interior affine mechanism family, and the informative three-observed-variable witness proves nonvacuity rather than completeness. The old isolated \(C_b\) bow is retained only as a regression baseline because its denominator \(1/2\) is structurally automatic. The open task is to derive a passing one- or two-mechanism tangent, or another exact rational lock, from every simultaneous branch failure. Failure of one template is not a counterexample. The no-selection specialization must collapse to CIDP. Continuous variables, intervention inputs, generic faithfulness, and finite-alphabet completeness beyond the explicit binary certificate subclass are outside scope.

seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the vacuous isolated-conditioning bow by a connected conditioning mechanism whose denominator equality is an exact parameter cancellation, and separate the algebraic compiler theorem from the still-open graph-to-rank implication.

seed_details.settled_vs_open: Exact compilation from a supplied affine rational fiber direction is finite linear algebra; existence of such a direction from every all-branches failure is open.
seed_details.closer-paper_check: No checked source gives a denominator-preserving rational countermodel compiler or an informative-denominator selected conditional hedge over a represented COPAG class.

literature_map: Chen and Mooij (2026) establish complete unconditional identification under selection for input-free COPAGs and give a sound conditional algorithm, while leaving conditional completeness open. Abouei, Mokhtarian, Kiyavash, and Grossglauser (2024) introduce selected counterparts of c-components and hedges for one known augmented ADMG and give a sound S-ID algorithm for an unconditional selected intervention target. Shpitser and Pearl (2006) give the fixed-graph complete conditional benchmark, and Jaber, Ribeiro, Zhang, and Bareinboim (2022) give the no-selection PAG benchmark. Duarte, Finkelstein, Knox, Mummolo, and Shpitser (2024) reduce discrete causal questions with confounding and selection to polynomial programs, but do not give a graph-native exact denominator-lock rank certificate or COPAG failure compiler. Hwang, Choe, Kwon, and Lee (2024) show why positivity obligations must follow the actual identifying formula and why naive denominator inspection can be too strong. Chen, Zoeter, and Mooij (2024) supply the conditioning-SCM semantics for selected populations. These threads leave open the exact passage from a failed selected conditional graph search to an informative denominator-preserving rational observational-fiber direction.

novelty_justification: The two closest results are Chen--Mooij's sound selected conditional algorithm and complete unconditional selected-COPAG algorithm, and Duarte--Finkelstein--Knox--Mummolo--Shpitser's polynomial-program representation of discrete causal fibers. The strict new object is an exact denominator-locked certificate compiler: on a supplied rational interior affine SCM template it characterizes, by a simplex-tangent rank condition, whether the complete selected observational law and a positive selected conditioning denominator can be held fixed while the selected joint numerator changes. A connected positive rational binary example shows that the lock can hold by informative selection cancellation rather than because the conditioning variable is isolated; a same-graph perturbation shows that the equality is not graph-forced. No checked source subsumes this object. The proposal does not claim that every failed Branch-sCIDP instance supplies a passing direction; that residual-forest-to-rank implication is the first-class open question.
